questions.question: Give three ways in which animals depend on plants.
questions.expected_answer: Animals depend on plants for food, such as leaves, fruit and nectar; for shelter, such as nests in branches or holes in trunks; and for oxygen, which green plants give off when they make food.

questions.question: Explain two ways in which plants depend on animals.
questions.expected_answer: Animals such as bees and sunbirds pollinate flowers by carrying pollen from one flower to another so that seeds can form. Animals such as elephants and birds spread seeds far away in their dung. Animals such as dung beetles and earthworms also add nutrients to the soil.

questions.question: Which non-living resources do plants and animals need, and what happens to a habitat if one of them changes?
questions.expected_answer: They need water, soil, air and sunlight. If one changes, for example a drought dries up the water, many plants and animals in the habitat are affected, because they all depend on each other.
